subject: social_science

concepts.title: Lithospheric Plates and Earth Movements
concepts.definition: Slabs of the Earth's crust move extremely slowly driven by thermal convection currents within mantle magma, dividing tectonic activity into endogenic and exogenic forces.
concepts.key_idea: Internal mantle convection propels crustal plate movement and drives endogenic and exogenic geological processes.
question_patterns: explain why lithospheric plates move slowly in Class 7 geography
differentiate between endogenic and exogenic forces on earth
what causes the movement of earth's lithospheric plates
classify forces that shape the earth's surface into internal and external types
describe how magma circulation affects crustal plate movement

solution_steps.action: Identify the driver of plate movement
solution_steps.explain: Recognize that heat convection in the earth's mantle causes circular movement of molten magma, shifting the overlying lithospheric plates.
Distinguish endogenic forces originating inside the earth (causing earthquakes and volcanoes) from exogenic forces operating on the surface (like wind and river erosion).

concepts.title: Volcanoes and Volcanic Eruptions
concepts.definition: A vent or opening in the earth's crust through which subterranean magma, molten rock, hot gases, and ash erupt suddenly.
concepts.key_idea: Deep subterranean pressure forces molten rock through crustal vents to form volcanic structures.
question_patterns: what is a volcano and what are its main components
explain how magma erupts through the earth's crust
identify the parts of a volcano including vent and crater
describe the sudden movement caused by endogenic volcanic activity
how does molten rock reach the surface during an eruption

solution_steps.action: Define a volcanic vent and magma chamber
solution_steps.explain: Locate the magma chamber deep underground and the vent or opening through which molten rock travels.
Trace how subterranean magma reaches the surface as lava along with released gases and ash forming a crater.

concepts.title: Earthquakes and Seismic Energy Transmission
concepts.definition: Sudden vibrations propagating through the earth caused by tectonic plate adjustments, originating at an underground focus and spreading outward from the surface epicentre.
concepts.key_idea: Tectonic vibrations radiate outward from the surface epicentre located directly above the subterranean origin focus.
question_patterns: distinguish between focus and epicentre of an earthquake
how do seismic waves travel through the earth
what causes the vibrations felt during an earthquake
identify the three main categories of seismic waves
explain where the maximum damage occurs during an earthquake event

solution_steps.explain: Define the focus as the subterranean point of energy release and epicentre as the point directly above it on the surface.
Understand that seismic energy radiates outward in waves, with peak intensity and damage nearest to the epicentre.

concepts.title: Earthquake Measurement and Disaster Preparedness
concepts.definition: Quantification of seismic magnitude using a seismograph on the Richter scale, alongside practical safety measures to mitigate disaster impacts.
concepts.key_idea: Richter scale rating measures earthquake magnitude while structural shelter precautions minimise human impact.
question_patterns: how is the magnitude of an earthquake measured
list safe spots to take shelter during an earthquake
what instrument records earthquake vibrations
explain the Richter scale classifications for earthquake intensity
describe precautions to stay safe during seismic activity

solution_steps.explain: Use a seismograph to detect ground vibrations and the Richter scale to assign numerical magnitude.
Seek shelter under sturdy furniture like desks or tables, avoid glass and fireplaces, and stay in clear indoor corners.

concepts.title: Weathering and Erosion Processes
concepts.definition: Degradation of surface geology split into static rock disintegration (weathering) and dynamic removal and transport of material by water, wind, or ice (erosion).
concepts.key_idea: Weathering breaks down surface rocks while natural agents erode, transport, and deposit rock particles to shape landforms.
question_patterns: differentiate between weathering and erosion
what agents are responsible for eroding the earth's landscape
explain how erosion and deposition continuously create new landforms
describe the process of rock disintegration on the earth's surface
how does landscape change over time due to exogenic processes

solution_steps.explain: Recognize weathering as the mechanical or chemical breaking down of stationary surface rocks.
Identify erosion as the removal and transport of sediment by water, wind, or ice, leading to deposition elsewhere.

concepts.title: Fluvial Landforms and River Processes
concepts.definition: Geological structures created across river courses, including erosion features like waterfalls and meanders, and deposition features like ox-bow lakes, floodplains, levees, and deltas.
concepts.key_idea: Running water shapes landscapes through upper-course erosion and lower-course deposition.
question_patterns: explain how an ox-bow lake is formed by a river
what features are formed by river deposition in plain regions
describe the formation of a waterfall and a delta
how are levees and floodplains developed during river flooding
differentiate between river meanders and distributaries

solution_steps.explain: Analyze steep gradient drops creating waterfalls and lateral erosion forming winding meanders.
Trace meander loop cut-offs forming ox-bow lakes, flood deposits forming fertile floodplains and levees, and river mouth sediments forming deltas.

concepts.title: Coastal Landforms and Sea Wave Action
concepts.definition: Shoreline structures produced by marine hydraulic action and abrasion, progressing from sea caves to arches and isolated stacks, along with sea cliffs and beaches.
concepts.key_idea: Continuous wave action erodes coastal rock from caves to arches and stacks, while sediment deposition creates beaches.
question_patterns: how do sea waves transform sea caves into stacks
explain the formation of beaches along coastal areas
describe the sequence of erosion from sea cave to sea arch and stack
what is a sea cliff and how is it formed
identify erosional and depositional landforms created by ocean waves

solution_steps.explain: Wave impact hollows out rock cracks to form sea caves, hollows out roofs to leave sea arches, and collapses roofs leaving vertical rock stacks.

solution_steps.action: Identify coastal deposition and cliff features
solution_steps.explain: Recognize steep rocky faces as sea cliffs and shoreline sediment accumulation as beaches.

concepts.title: Glacial Landforms and Ice Erosion
concepts.definition: Features crafted by moving ice sheets that scrape bedrock hollows which fill into glacial lakes, while dumping mixed rock sediment as glacial moraines.
concepts.key_idea: Moving glaciers carve deep bedrock hollows and deposit unsorted rock debris known as moraines.
question_patterns: what are glaciers and how do they alter the landscape
how are glacial moraines formed
explain how mountain lakes are created by glacial action
describe the erosional process known as bulldozing by rivers of ice
identify depositional features resulting from melting glaciers

solution_steps.explain: Glaciers scrape underlying bedrock through bulldozing action, carving deep depressions that hold meltwater lakes.
Melting ice leaves behind piles of boulders, gravel, sand, and silt called glacial moraines.

concepts.title: Aeolian Landforms and Wind Action
concepts.definition: Arid features shaped by wind erosion and transport, producing narrow-based mushroom rocks, shifting sand dunes, and extensive fine silt loess deposits.
concepts.key_idea: Desert winds selectively erode rock bases and deposit sand as dunes or fine dust as extensive loess fields.
question_patterns: why do some desert rocks have the shape of a mushroom
explain how sand dunes are formed in desert landscapes
what is loess and where are large deposits of loess found
describe the active agents of erosion and deposition in deserts
differentiate between sand dunes and loess deposits

solution_steps.explain: Wind erodes lower rock sections more aggressively than upper parts, forming mushroom-shaped rocks.
Lighter sand particles drop when wind stops to form sand dunes, while fine silt travels far to deposit as loess.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Differentiate between endogenic and exogenic forces shaping the Earth's surface.

solution_template.explain: Endogenic forces are internal geological forces originating deep within the earth that cause sudden events like earthquakes and volcanoes or slow mountain-building movements.
Exogenic forces act on the earth's surface through natural agents like running water, wind, sea waves, and ice that continuously erode and deposit material.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain the difference between focus and epicentre during an earthquake.

solution_template.explain: The focus is the location inside the earth's crust where tectonic movement begins and seismic energy is released.
The epicentre is the point on the earth's surface located directly vertically above the focus, where seismic waves first hit and cause maximum destruction.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Describe how an ox-bow lake is formed by a river.

solution_template.explain: As a river flows through a plain, lateral erosion and deposition form large looping bends called meanders.
Continuous erosion brings the ends of a meander loop closer together until the river cuts through the narrow neck, abandoning the bend to form a crescent-shaped ox-bow lake.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Give reasons why mushroom rocks are narrow at the base and wider at the top.

solution_template.action: Analyze wind erosion behavior in deserts
solution_template.explain: Desert winds carry sand grains close to the ground, concentrating maximum abrasive power at lower rock levels.
Because the lower section erodes faster than the upper section, the standing rock develops a narrow base and broad top resembling a mushroom.
